equity_bridge.item: Investment securities at fair value (strategic shareholdings, AFS)
equity_bridge.note: FY2026 Securities Report consolidated balance sheet, 2026-03-31; dividend income from these holdings is stripped from the flows (matching-asset rule).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_7yr_precovid_cagr (FY2019 -> FY2026, 4.3%) rounded; equity and EPS CAGRs rejected as recovery-distorted
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: 3-year and 5-year CAGRs are COVID-recovery artefacts: FY2021 revenue collapsed to JPY 170.6bn (park closures) and FY2023 was still 8% below FY2019. Equity 5-yr CAGR 7.7% exceeds the pre-COVID revenue trend by >30% because retained earnings rebuilt from a loss base. 5-yr EPS and FCF CAGRs are undefined (negative FY2021 base: EPS -33.1, FCF -140.8bn).
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less interest and dividend income; SBC is nil throughout). Owner FCF FY2019 JPY 51.0bn -> FY2023 JPY 74.4bn -> FY2026 JPY 93.8bn; the FY2019-FY2020 figures are depressed by Fantasy Springs capex (FY2020 reported FCF -61.0bn), so even the pre-COVID FCF CAGR flatters the trend. Reported-FCF 3-yr CAGR 9.4% vs owner-FCF 8.0%: the gap is the interest on the growing cash pile (JPY 3.9bn FY2026 vs JPY 0.1bn FY2023), not SBC.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 modestly beats cautious guidance; capacity-managed parks compound per-guest spend at 3-4% with inbound a rising share; 2027 Tokyo Disneyland attractions and the FYE Mar-2029 cruise launch add two years of 7-8% growth; EBITDA margin settles at 34% and capex normalises to 11% of revenue after the ship is paid for. Owner FCF: JPY 20-40bn through FY2029, JPY 130bn+ thereafter.
scenario_narratives.bull: Q1 FY2027 run-rate persists, inbound tailwind continues, attendance ceiling lifted modestly, per-guest spend +5-6%, cruise ship sells out at park-beating margins and a second ship follows; EBITDA margin 36%, terminal growth 2.0%.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY2027 lands on guidance, then inbound shock or single-site disruption, flat per-guest spend against rising wages, cruise late and under-loaded; EBITDA margin 31%, committed capex spent anyway, 15x terminal cap, terminal growth 1.0%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Oriental Land is valued as a mature, capacity-constrained operating company on owner free cash flow: reported FCF less the interest and dividends earned on the JPY 597bn liquid pile (added back in the bridge with the JPY 59bn investment-securities portfolio). The COVID collapse (FY2021-FY2022) is excluded from every trend used: growth is anchored on the FY2019-to-FY2026 pre-COVID-to-now revenue CAGR of 4.3%, not the 3- or 5-year recovery CAGRs, and year 1 is anchored on the company's FY2027 forecast and Q1 run-rate. Near-term FCF is deliberately not the FY2026 figure carried forward: the committed JPY 330bn cruise ship, JPY 70.5bn Space Mountain and JPY 29.5bn Wreck-It Ralph projects push capex to 20-27% of revenue for three years, so owner FCF falls to roughly zero before recovering; the 10-year horizon exists so the terminal year capitalises a normalised 11% capex rate, not the build phase. The terminal value is capped at 20x owner FCF (15x bear) while the market pays 46x trailing EPS and 57x EV/owner FCF; the resulting gap between weighted IV and price is the scarcity premium the market assigns to a monopoly Disney licence in Japan, reported rather than assumed away. SBC is nil, so house and street bases coincide and band_position is null.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cruise ship: JPY 330bn committed with no operating history; a late, over-budget or under-loaded launch removes two years of growth and the margin step-up (bear case).

Single-site concentration: both parks, all hotels and Ikspiari sit on one reclaimed-land site in Urayasu; a major Kanto earthquake or extended closure has no diversifying offset until the ship operates.
Inbound dependence: per-guest spend growth since FY2023 leans on overseas visitors and a weak yen; yen appreciation or regional geopolitics reverses it.
Pricing elasticity: attendance is held flat by choice; if domestic guests resist further price increases the growth model has no volume lever.
Disney licence economics: royalties are a fixed share of revenue under agreements running to 2051; any renegotiation is outside the company's control.
Management's FY2029 operating-cash-flow target (~JPY 300bn) sits well above the base case; if it is delivered the base case is too low, and the bull weight understates it.
Guidance vintage: FY2027 forecast and Q1 are taken from Analysis.json; the H1 FY2027 tanshin (due ~2026-10-30) is not yet extracted and should be checked at the next update.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (TSE regular close); 52-week range 2103-3450 JPY.
data_sources.financials: research/4661.T/Reports/4661.T_Metrics.csv (financial-parser, FY2008-FY2026 + interims, JPY millions, post-split share basis); FY2026 Securities Report (balance sheet p.69-70, cash flow p.74-75, capex pipeline p.2205-2222 and facilities table p.2527); H1 FY2026 tanshin (2025-10-30) for the FY2026 forecast and interim run-rate.
data_sources.qualitative: research/4661.T/Reports/4661.T_Analysis.json (qualitative-analyst, 2026-10-31: FY2027 guidance, Q1 FY2027 results, 2035 long-term strategy targets, bull/bear axes); FY2026 Securities Report business policy and risk sections (cruise business, single-site, inbound, cost of capex).

inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Securities Report: no share-based payment line in the cash flow statement; the only equity plan is a small trust-based executive remuneration scheme (provision JPY 303m at 2026-03-31). SBC treated as zero and kept explicit at 0% of revenue; StockBasedComp = 0 backfilled into Metrics.csv FY2008-FY2026 via make fix.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2026 financing: purchase of treasury shares JPY 0 (FY2025: JPY 61,830m). Buybacks are episodic (FY2017-18, FY2020, FY2025); the flat count is a modelling convention and is not being funded in FY2026.
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,639.508m = shares outstanding net of treasury per the FY2026 Securities Report / Metrics.csv (1,800.45m issued less 156.8m treasury = 1,643.6m; the CSV figure additionally nets ~4.1m trust-held executive-plan shares, matching the EPS denominator). Held FLAT: SBC is nil and buybacks are value-neutral in this model. Post 5-for-1 split (April 2023) basis throughout.
inputs.cash_definition: Wide liquid-asset base: cash and deposits JPY 468,214m + current securities (short-term bonds/CP held to maturity) JPY 128,884m = JPY 597,098m at 2026-03-31. Narrow cash-and-equivalents is JPY 236,132m; the JPY 361bn difference is time deposits >3 months and short-dated securities, all held as 'temporary surplus funds in highly liquid financial assets' pending the cruise capex (yuho p.5915). The wide base is correct because the interest it earns (JPY 2,834m interest + JPY 1,072m dividends = JPY 3,906m) is stripped from the flows.
inputs.debt_definition: Bonds payable JPY 310,000m (20,000 current + 290,000 non-current, incl. JPY 100bn issued Oct-2025 under the JPY 300bn shelf) + long-term loans JPY 16,706m = JPY 326,706m. Lease obligations JPY 237m excluded as immaterial.
inputs.wacc_rationale: JPY-denominated build. 10-year JGB ~1.6% (Oct-2026), Japan ERP 5.5%, beta 0.9 (low-beta domestic consumer franchise) gives cost of equity ~6.55%; pre-tax cost of debt ~1.2% (Oct-2025 bond coupons), ~0.85% after 30.6% tax; market-value weights ~94% equity / 6% debt give ~6.2%, rounded to 6.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: single-site concentration, inbound-demand cyclicality and cruise execution are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: J-GAAP filer; operating leases are expensed within operating costs and finance-lease obligations are JPY 237m. No lease adjustment: nothing deducted from flows beyond the P&L charge, nothing added to net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: No non-controlling interests (comprehensive income attributable to NCI is nil). Flows are 100% attributable.
inputs.excluded_income_matching_assets: Stripped JPY 3,906m interest and dividend income; matching assets are the JPY 597,098m liquid base (in net debt) and JPY 59,306m investment securities at fair value (in equity_bridge). Equity-method profit (JPY 440m) left in the flows as immaterial.
inputs.guidance_status: FY2027 (FYE 2027-03-31) company forecast, issued April 2026 and reaffirmed with Q1 in July 2026 (per Analysis.json; the tanshin PDFs themselves are not in the extracted set): net sales JPY 724,312m (+2.8%), operating profit JPY 160,776m (-4.5%, hotel renovation costs from Q2 and higher personnel/maintenance), DPS JPY 16 (from 14). Q1 FY2027 actual: net sales JPY 180,734m (+10.4%), operating profit JPY 47,716m (+23.1%), attendance +7% and per-guest spend +5% on the DisneySea 25th anniversary; the Q1 net profit includes a one-off gain on the sale of the Hyatt Regency Seragaki Island Okinawa. Management beat its own FY2026 forecast by 1.6% on sales and 5.3% on operating profit. Medium/long-term targets: operating cash flow (net profit + D&A) ~JPY 300bn in FY2029 (FY2026: JPY 188bn) and net sales >= JPY 1tn by FY2035. H1 FY2027 results (due ~2026-10-30) not yet on file.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US' plus owner-fcf-adaptations: JPY WACC, SBC-zero, J-GAAP leases, matching-asset rule). Oriental Land operates Tokyo Disneyland and Tokyo DisneySea under licence from Disney (royalty-bearing, agreements to September 2051 with five-year extensions), plus Disney hotels and Ikspiari; Theme Park segment >80% of sales and profit. Attendance is deliberately capacity-managed at ~27.5m (FY2024-FY2026 flat; FY2019 peak 32.6m) and growth is per-guest spend (JPY 17,833 FY2025 vs JPY 11,815 FY2019) driven by variable pricing, Premier Access and inbound visitors. Historical growth rates straddling FY2020-FY2022 are COVID-distorted: FY2021 revenue JPY 170.6bn on park closures; the 7-year pre-COVID-to-now revenue CAGR (4.3%) is the usable trend, not the 5-year (32.8%). Capex is in a second supercycle: after Fantasy Springs (JPY 320bn, opened Jun-2024) the committed pipeline is Space Mountain redevelopment JPY 70.5bn (JPY 27bn remaining, 2027), Wreck-It Ralph attraction JPY 29.5bn (spring 2027) and the first Disney cruise ship JPY 330bn (JPY 306bn remaining, service in FYE Mar-2029), so capex runs 20-27% of revenue in FY2027-FY2029 before normalising to ~11%. Current price implies 46x trailing EPS, 22.8x EV/EBITDA and 57x EV/owner FCF; a 20x terminal FCF cap cannot reproduce that multiple, which is the gap the valuation reports rather than closes. The price is a regular TSE close, not after-hours.

bear.narrative: FY2027 lands on the cautious guidance (+2.8% sales, OP -4.5%) as a weak H2 and hotel renovations absorb the Q1 anniversary surge; thereafter inbound demand stalls (yen strength, geopolitics or a Kanto earthquake closing the single Maihama site for a period) and domestic guests push back on pricing, so per-guest spend goes flat while labour and energy costs keep rising and the Disney royalty stays fixed as a share of revenue; the cruise ship arrives late and over budget, loads at 70% and dilutes group margins to 31%. The JPY 330bn is spent regardless, so FY2027-FY2029 owner FCF is near zero. Terminal cap 15x reflects a market that stops paying a scarcity premium.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 5.0% (FY2027): company guides +2.8% (JPY 724.3bn) but Q1 ran +10.4% on the DisneySea 25th anniversary and management has a record of guiding low (FY2026 beat by 1.6%); 5% sits between the reaffirmed guidance and the Q1 run-rate, allowing for the weather-sensitive H2 and hotel renovation downtime management cites. Y2 5.0%: Space Mountain and Wreck-It Ralph open in 2027 (first full year FY2028). Y3 7.0% / Y4 8.0%: cruise ship enters service in FYE Mar-2029 (partial year) then first full year (~JPY 60-70bn revenue at full run-rate, 4,000-berth ship). Y5+ tapers to 2.5% (Japan nominal GDP plus pricing). Y9 revenue (FY2035) lands at ~JPY 1.05tn, consistent with the company's FY2035 target of JPY 1tn or more.
base.margin_rationale: Y1 EBITDA margin 32.5%: guidance implies ~31.9% (OP JPY 160.8bn, -4.5%, plus ~JPY 70bn D&A) on personnel, maintenance and hotel renovation costs; 32.5% allows the same modest beat as the top line. FY2026 actual 33.3% (FY2025 35.0%, FY2024 34.3%). Y2 33.0% as renovations complete, dips to 32.5% in the cruise launch year on pre-opening costs, recovers to 34.0% once the ship ('higher profitability than the Theme Park Segment' per management) is at run-rate. The company's own FY2029 operating-cash-flow target of ~JPY 300bn would need an operating margin in the mid-30s; the base case does not assume it is met, the bull case approaches it. D&A rises from 9.45% to 10.5% as Space Mountain and the JPY 330bn ship start depreciating. Capex: FY2027-FY2029 carry the JPY 306bn cruise balance plus JPY 50bn park projects on top of ~JPY 65bn maintenance/content, then 11% of revenue (above D&A) for continuous reinvestment and a possible second ship. Cash tax 30.5% = FY2025-FY2026 actual cash rate.
base.narrative: Tokyo Disney Resort keeps attendance near 27.5m by design and compounds per-guest spend at 3-4% a year through variable pricing and premium products, with inbound visitors a rising share; FY2027 modestly beats a deliberately cautious forecast, the 2027 Tokyo Disneyland attractions add modest demand, and the first cruise ship launches on schedule in FYE Mar-2029 and reaches run-rate in its first full year. Owner FCF is suppressed to JPY 20-40bn in FY2027-FY2029 by the ship build and then steps up to JPY 130bn+ as capex normalises.

bull.narrative: The Q1 FY2027 run-rate (+10.4% sales, +23% OP) proves closer to the year than the guidance; inbound tourism keeps growing on a weak yen and the company lifts the attendance ceiling modestly with the new Tokyo Disneyland areas while per-guest spend compounds 5-6% on premium access and hotel pricing; the cruise ship sells out at JPY 90-100bn revenue with margins above the parks and a second ship is ordered, taking group EBITDA margin to 36% and bringing the FY2029 JPY 300bn operating-cash-flow target within reach. Same committed capex, higher revenue over it.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 20% for single-site concentration (one resort in Urayasu, Kanto seismic exposure) and a thesis now resting on an unproven cruise business that absorbs JPY 330bn before a yen of revenue. Bull cut to 25% because it needs inbound growth, a lifted attendance ceiling, pricing without volume loss and a sold-out ship to all go right together. Base 55%: the parks have a 40-year record of pricing power and management beat its own FY2026 guidance on sales and operating profit, and Q1 FY2027 was a record.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
